author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Automattic confirmed Saturday that WordPress co-founder Matt Mullenweg has returned as chairman and chief executive after a board vote placed him on paid leave earlier in the week. A company spokesperson told TechCrunch that Mullenweg had the board’s full support, reversing the leadership arrangement announced days earlier.

Automattic had said Wednesday that Chief Financial Officer Mark Davies would serve as interim CEO while Mullenweg was on leave. TechCrunch reported that Mullenweg resisted the move and told employees he was back in control. The company’s latest statement formally resolves the chief executive question for now, though the reasons for the original leave remain undisclosed.

Questions also remain about Automattic’s board composition. TechCrunch said it had sought comment on reports that board member and former Automattic CEO Toni Schneider stepped down, but had not received confirmation. The episode creates an unusual governance moment for the company behind WordPress.com and other publishing, commerce and messaging products.
dek: The WordPress.com parent said its founder again has the board’s support days after directors placed him on paid leave.
headline: Automattic confirms Matt Mullenweg has returned as CEO
